proposals.title: Long videos are blocked on this long-first channel by the Paisa 'from_short' rule
proposals.change: In generator/topics.py winning_short(): for a channel whose channel.json has cadence.longEveryHours (long-first, each Short a promo of a long video; disasters-and-engineering-failures-expla), do not require from_short; or let a long topic name from_short only when the channel's recipe says long videos expand Shorts. Since v-20261121-42 was published on 21 Nov, `python -m generator.run state --channel disasters-and-engineering-failures-expla --format long` blocks every long topic ('names no from_short'), so the owner's 'one long video every 48 hours' cannot run. Add a test with a long-first channel fixture.
evidence: generator/topics.py winning_short(): the 'new channel with no Short' exception ends once any Short is in metrics/videos.json
state --format long on 2026-11-22: 0 of 4 long videos this week; 2026-11-20-hyatt-walkways blocked_by 'names no from_short'
channels/disasters-and-engineering-failures-expla/profile.md: long videos one every 48 hours, each with one promo Short
proposals.expectedEffect: Long videos can be planned again; promo Shorts get their long video
proposals.risk: channel #1 must keep its rule: gate the exception on the channel's own cadence
proposals.reason: Already fixed on main on 22 Nov (522702a: a long topic never needs one of our Shorts, on any channel).

proposals.title: Famous-passenger crashes: tell the report's mechanism, not the celebrity
proposals.change: For the three topics added tonight with a famous person aboard (Calabasas S-76B, the Long-EZ, the Convair 240), the writer names the person once as the NTSB does, states deaths once, and spends the Short on the mechanism (inner ear in a turn, a handle behind the shoulder, a fuel gauge against the map). The fact reviewer checks the report's own probable-cause words. No new code: a note for the writer and QA when these topics are taken.
proposals.expectedEffect: Flight Simulator's famous-flight Shorts run 13-68x its 158K subscribers; done with respect they stay ad-friendly and inside the profile's 'cause, not gore' line.
proposals.risk: Reads as exploiting a celebrity death if the title leads with the name and the toll; keep the title on the machine.
proposals.reason: A note for three particular topics belongs on those topics in the feed (research adds it to their `verify`/notes, which the writer and fact reviewer read); the profile's cause-not-gore rule and the title rule already cover it, and a general writer change would be a recipe change for the weekly loop.

proposals.title: Long videos: name the event plus one concrete stake in the title, and cut the thumbnail from the 3D reconstruction
proposals.change: For long videos only (Studio's title and thumbnail step), test on alternate long videos: (A) title = '<stake with one sourced figure or moment> | <Event name> <year>' or '<Event name>: <question>', always naming the event as people search it (e.g. 'The Last Text Before 25 People Died | Chatsworth Train Crash'); add 'in 3D' / 'Rebuilt in 3D' when the video has the three-kit reconstruction. (B) thumbnail = a frame of the type-accurate 3D shot of the actual vehicle or structure at the moment of failure with the failing part ringed in red and at most 3 words, instead of the flat cartoon. The 3D label rule still applies on screen. Measure impressions CTR and views7d per long video on each side.
proposals.expectedEffect: More search and browse clicks on long videos, which are at 0-15 views after 1-4 days. Small-channel breakouts in this week's scan all name the event and most promise 3D: Fatal Chain Chatsworth 9.6K on 606 subs (15.8x), Last Altitude 'Every Clue Rebuilt in 3D' 31K on 1.68K (18x), Time of Impact Germanwings 'Final 10 Minutes' 17.8K on 397 (45x).
proposals.risk: Event names can read as news-bait; keep the report's words and no gore or victim imagery in the thumbnail (limited ads).
proposals.reason: Testing the title half as long experiment dd-long-title-3d (on views in 7 days, 4 a side, up to 42 days): 'Rebuilt in 3D' after the event's name. The stake-first title breaks the owner's 23 Nov name-first rule; the 3D thumbnail waits for the next long test (one change at a time).

proposals.title: Re-check the long-video tiers of corner_cut_structure and air_crash_rule against their biggest references
proposals.change: formats.json marks corner_cut_structure and air_crash_rule tier 'low' (from the 20 Nov title scan, whose medians are dragged down by tiny channels). Their single biggest references are larger than any core long format's: Taum Sauk by Practical Engineering about 11.2M views on about 4.8M subscribers (2.3x), and Asiana 214 by Mentour Pilot about 4.6M on about 2.5M (1.8x), against stunt_gone_wrong's best of 1.23M. Because research must keep two in three added topics core, these two formats almost never get new long topics (tonight: none). Improver: when our long videos have views7d per format (4+ per side), compare corner_cut_structure and air_crash_rule with the core formats and move a tier only on our own numbers; until then, test by letting Studio pick one of the open corner_cut_structure topics (FIU bridge, Oroville, Ronan Point) next. 2026-11-28: more air-crash demand in the 27 Nov scan (Darkside Dispatch's Asiana 214 Short 115.3K on 762 subscribers, 151x; its BA38 Short 53.8K on 762, 71x).
proposals.expectedEffect: More long topics in formats whose top references reach millions, if our own long numbers agree.
proposals.risk: The view counts are third-party snapshots (YouTube's own pages refused the read); our long videos have 10-15 views each, too few to judge any format yet.
